title: Maya Ara: a practical, low-density freehold in Ara Damansara.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #439 | MAYA ARA, ARA DAMANSARA
excerpt: A completed 381-unit freehold project surrounded by landed homes, where open-air lobbies and a no-frills facility deck put practicality and low maintenance first.
takeaways: Only 381 freehold units, with landed homes all around and shops within walking distance.
Open-air lobbies, transparent car park doors and naturally ventilated corridors.
Puzzling level changes on the facility deck, and uncertainty over two neighbouring plots.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Maya Ara has just 381 units on freehold land, in two wings with 17 units a floor sharing four lifts. The drop-off, lobbies and corridors are open air, so they need no aircon, and the car park lift lobbies have transparent doors. The facility deck on level eight faces away from the main road, with a half basketball court, a games room, an infinity pool and a Technogym gym.

Sean viewed a 764 sq ft, two-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with no balcony, wide windows and an aircon ledge set low, out of sight. Its 3.5 m wide second bedroom and centrally placed master bedroom suit a couple, or one person working from home.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project faces a five-lane road through Ara Damansara, buffered by an internal road and landscaping, near Seri Pilmoor. It is one junction from the Subang Airport highway, close to the bridge to Bandar Utama and a shortcut to PJ, with Ara Damansara and Lembah Subang LRT stations, Citta Mall and Sunway Pyramid nearby. Two commercial areas and the Ara Damansara mosque are walkable.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Sean reads subsale listings at about RM850 to RM900 psf, with one at RM690,000, and fully furnished rents of about RM2,800 to RM3,100 a month. At around RM650,000 and RM3,000 rent, he says the numbers are not bad, and early buyers have already made money on the launch price.

standout.title: A car park lobby built for safety
standout.body: The lift lobbies on the car park floors are open air, so they need no aircon, and their doors are transparent, so children can see cars before stepping out. Sean ranks it among his top three car park lobbies, and says residents use it far more than the grand entrance.

pros: The Ara Damansara address: between the Bandar Utama bridge, the airport highway and PJ, with two LRT stations, two mature commercial areas within walking distance, and low-rise landed homes all around for views.
Low density: only 381 units, so the project feels quiet, from a developer whose other nearby launch also sold out.
Practical design: open-air lobbies that cut maintenance, ventilation blocks, a facility deck away from road noise, and landscape islands that create an illusion of density.
cons: The main road: less of a problem than Sean expected, thanks to the internal road and landscaping. Driving within Ara Damansara is fine; getting in and out of it is the issue.
Unexplained level changes on the facility deck, with ramps and steps around the gym on a flat site.
Uncertainty over two adjacent plots, likely to become more mid-rise housing. Sean says owners who bought at the launch price need not fear new projects.

closing: Sean loves the unit and says he regrets not buying one himself.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this April 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the completed unit; prices and rents are from property portal listings. The unit was furnished under a package with The Makeover Guys, a furnishing company Sean works with, which he says had some hiccups before completion.
